premises: Defects and oxygen impurities create additional scattering channels that strongly influence electronic conductivity in HfNbTaTiZr.
Standard analytical models assume ideal, defect-free crystals and thus miss these scattering mechanisms.
A simulation method integrating realistic defect distributions and oxygen effects can be developed and applied to conductivity calculations.
Such a method will yield conductivity estimates within ~10% of experiment across 0–200 K and 300–1200 K.
The approach is reliable for bulk HfNbTaTiZr with up to 1 wt.% oxygen from near 0 K to 1200 K.
